name: Phenylpropanolamine

overview.mechanism: Historically used for oral nasal decongestion and appetite suppression; renal elimination is important to systemic exposure [[PPA-STROKE,PPA-PK]].
uses: Historical decongestant and appetite-suppressant use is described for context. FDA removed PPA from US OTC use after hemorrhagic-stroke safety concerns; this is not a recommendation to use it [[PPA-FDA]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Case-control study: 702 hemorrhagic-stroke cases and 1,376 controls, ages 18–49.
rows.findings: Among women, appetite-suppressant exposure was associated with hemorrhagic stroke (adjusted odds ratio 16.58; 95% CI 1.51–182.21). First-use association estimate was 3.13 (0.86–11.46).
rows.limitations: Observational association, sparse exposures and wide confidence intervals; the first-use estimate was not statistically significant. Absence of a demonstrated subgroup association does not establish safety.

rows.design: Pharmacokinetic study in eight healthy volunteers.
rows.findings: Mean unchanged urinary recovery was 86%; investigators advised caution with impaired renal function.
rows.limitations: Healthy volunteers; not a renal dose-finding or dialysis study.

sources.citation: FDA Nonprescription Drugs Advisory Committee briefing document, September 11–12, 2023: regulatory history of oral nasal decongestants, including phenylpropanolamine.
Phenylpropanolamine and the risk of hemorrhagic stroke. PubMed PMID: 11117973.
Steady-state kinetics of sustained-release phenylpropanolamine. PubMed PMID: 6698658.
The effects of urine pH modification on the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of phenylpropanolamine. PubMed PMID: 2300545.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

serious: Hemorrhagic stroke is the central regulatory safety concern; FDA history records removal from OTC use following the safety analysis [[PPA-FDA,PPA-STROKE]].

key_interactions.effect: A small healthy-volunteer study found lower renal PPA clearance, higher postabsorptive exposure and higher diastolic blood pressure with alkalinization [[PPA-PH]].
key_interactions.action: Recognize this exposure interaction during medication review; the study does not provide a safe compensating dose [[PPA-PH]].

renal: Extensive unchanged renal elimination raises concern in renal impairment; the cited study advises caution but supplies no CKD or dialysis dosing algorithm [[PPA-PK]].
